ov: Three species of striped wild horse: the plains, Grévy’s and mountain zebras of eastern and southern Africa. Every zebra’s stripe pattern is unique.

why.dg: Zebras bite and kick hard, and can turn aggressive, especially when defending their young.
why.dm: Never domesticated. Colonial-era attempts to ride and drive them in East Africa had little success.

rg: Plains zebras across the savannas of eastern and southern Africa, Grévy’s zebras in the dry north-east, and mountain zebras in the south-west.

src.title: Animal Diversity Web: Equus burchellii (plains zebra)

_cf.tip: Despite the striped legs, the okapi isn’t related to zebras.
A zonkey is shaped and coloured like a donkey, with zebra stripes mainly on its legs and belly rather than all over.
